newsitem.title: EGYPT: Cairo court jails ex-chairman for corruption.
newsitem.headline: Cairo court jails ex-chairman for corruption.

text.p: An Egyptian court on Monday sentenced the former head of a public sector firm to 10 years in jail and ordered him to pay a total of $50 million for taking millions of dollars in commissions, court sources said.
The court fined Abdelwahab el-Habbak, former chairman of the Holding Company for Engineering Industries, $25 million and ordered him to repay the state another $25 million, they said.
If Habbak does not pay the $50 million, he will spend one extra day in jail for each unpaid 0.50 pounds ($0.15), the sources said.
While reading the verdict, the judge said: "The case has political dimensions, as other officials are involved. Habbak is the only person who knows their names."
Habbak has been convicted of charges including appropriating 91 million pounds by illegal means during his 11-year career with the public firm. He retired last year.

He has made headlines in Egypt since he was detained for questioning by the anti-corruption squad in September 1996 and reportedly offered to repay the government $19 million from his Swiss bank accounts.
The Holding Company for Engineering Industries is parent company to 21 state manufacturing firms, several of which are listed for early privatisation.
